take_homes: Access and absorption are different numbers. Counting licences or logins says nothing about whether people use the thing.

Before I roll anything out, ask the person what would have to be true for them to drop what they use now. Pick the obstacle that makes the others hard, and name who owns, maintains and governs the thing.
Go and talk to one person before building more.

monday.move: Ask one sales lead how they prepare for a customer call today, before I build any sales-team setup. Also name who would maintain it.
monday.who: one sales lead, probably the one who already uses our CRM notes a lot
monday.when: Monday or Tuesday, a 20 minute chat, likely after I've already sketched the agent on Sunday
monday.stop_condition: if they say they already have a way that works, or nobody on their side wants to own it, I don't build it
monday.blocker: I'll want to build first, and nobody outside engineering has asked for this yet. I don't know who would maintain it.

misconception.why: The module never made me check the agent's output. The spot-check lines read like ceremony, I skipped them, and the module didn't catch it. The 'empty people plan' line and the failed decision in the story did shake my belief that a good build gets used, which is related but not the same. I still think checking is for beginners.

one_line: Nothing new on the agent side, but 'access is not absorption' and 'what would have to be true for them to switch' are going to stick, and I wish it had been shorter. The identical 'a note on context' filler three times is annoying.
